title: How Dagobert Renouf learned to start from audience problems after Logology stalled
summary: Dagobert Renouf recounts building Logology with his wife, years of slow traction, and how Twitter changed his marketing and mood. He explains why his audience-first Twitter course beat the product-first Logology, and how he will rebuild Logology 2 around his audience's problems.

principles.text: Start from an audience and its problems, then build the product, instead of building first and hunting for buyers.
principles.quote: we're going to start with people's problem so I have my audience I mean my audience know like those people who follow me let's say and I just need to figure out their problem

principles.text: Sharing your own founder journey draws in fellow founders and works as soft, non-salesy customer acquisition.
principles.quote: just talking about my startup and my journey is enough to make startup Founders notice and engage and then you know after some time they get curious they check out my startup and boom

principles.text: Engage with others first; their topics fuel your best ideas, and good replies get repurposed into tweets and memes.
principles.quote: Step Zero is engage with other people because that's how I get the best ideas

principles.text: Combine authenticity with deliberate strategy rather than posting whatever you feel like.
principles.quote: I try to mix authenticity with strategy that's always been like my balance

principles.text: Be generous and self-promotional in a daily rhythm: help others first, then push your own content.
principles.quote: I'm selfless in the morning and selfish in the evening basically in the morning I engage with other people's content and in the evening it's only my tweets that matter

principles.text: Choose a co-founder you could raise a child with, since a startup forces you to confront everything under pressure.
principles.quote: you should pick someone you could have a baby with
